What Is a Quarterly Business Review (QBR)?

Explainerlowob research

By lowob · 10 November 2026 · 5-minute read · Revenue

A quarterly business review (QBR) is a meeting held every three months in which a supplier and a customer review results against the goals they agreed, discuss what has changed in the customer's business and set goals for the next quarter. Its purpose is to keep both sides agreed on the value being delivered, well before a renewal date. A QBR that only presents usage statistics is a report, not a review. The test is whether the customer leaves with decisions and owners.

What a quarterly business review means

A QBR is part of account management, not support. It sits between day-to-day contact and the renewal conversation. Gainsight's guide lists five core elements: a review of performance against agreed goals using data, a discussion of the customer's challenges and changes, joint goal-setting for the next quarter, a demonstration of value including return on investment, and next steps with owners and timelines.

The term is used loosely. Three related meetings are often confused.

MeetingWho attends (customer side)FocusTypical frequency
QBRManagers, team leads and active usersProgress against goals, usage, issues, next quarter's goalsEvery three months
Executive business review (EBR)C-suite, vice presidents and directorsBusiness outcomes and strategic valueEvery six months for strategic accounts; yearly for growth accounts (Gainsight)
Renewal value reviewSponsor and decision makersWhat the term achieved and what the next term should deliverOnce, about 120 days before renewal in lowob's calendar

For new customers, Gainsight suggests the first EBR after initial value is realised, typically three to six months after implementation. Not every account needs a quarterly meeting; smaller accounts can get a lighter digital review.

Why it matters for a commercial team

Buyers often regret what they bought

Gartner's 2023 survey, run from February to March across North America, Western Europe and Asia/Pacific, found 60% of technology buyers involved in renewal or expansion decisions regret nearly every purchase. Gartner attributes most of that regret to dysfunction inside distributed buying teams, not to the supplier or the product. Its recommendations include training customer-facing teams to spot regret signals, such as buyers revisiting decisions or internal conflict, and giving buying teams shared spaces to review objectives and build business cases.

A QBR is the natural place to do both, while there is still time to act.

Growth is expected from the existing base

Gartner's 2025 survey of chief sales officers found 73% focused on growing revenue from existing customers, and 57% ranked retention and growth among their top three priorities. Renewals and Expansion sets out why: for most mid-size B2B firms the existing base barely grows on its own. QBRs are where the evidence for an expansion is built, in the customer's terms.

A QBR that shows usage charts is a report. A QBR that ends with agreed goals, owners and dates is a review.

How to run one

SectionWhat to bringWhat to leave with
Goals from last quarterThe goals agreed at the last review, with resultsEach goal marked met, missed or changed, with the reason
Customer changesQuestions about strategy, people and budgetUpdated sponsor and stakeholder list
Value deliveredOutcomes in the customer's measures, not product metricsAn agreed statement of value for the quarter
IssuesOpen support cases and risksOwners and dates for each
Next quarterProposed goalsTwo or three goals the customer has agreed
Next stepsA draft action listActions with owners on both sides

Three habits separate useful QBRs from routine ones. Send a short pre-read so the meeting is spent on decisions. Let the customer present part of it, so the value statement is theirs. Keep it to an hour, as Gainsight advises.

In lowob's model, the goals agreed at a QBR are decisions with a reason, an owner, a status and an expected outcome. The next QBR is the natural point for outcome write-back: each goal is graded against what happened. Over a year, that record becomes the renewal case, and it feeds the customer health score with evidence rather than impressions. An agent can draft the pre-read from CRM, usage and support data at autonomy level 1. A person checks and presents it, and nothing goes to the customer without that review.

lowob takeaways

  • A QBR is a review, not a report. It should end with agreed goals, owners and dates.
  • It is an early warning system. Sponsor changes and internal conflict surface here before renewal.
  • Match the meeting to the account. QBRs for the top tier, EBRs for executives, lighter reviews for the rest.
  • Grade last quarter's goals. The written record of goals and results becomes the renewal case.

Common questions

What should be included in a quarterly business review?

Results against last quarter's goals, changes in the customer's business, the value delivered in the customer's terms, open issues, and agreed goals and actions for the next quarter.

What is the difference between a QBR and an EBR?

A QBR reviews progress and usage with managers and users every quarter. An executive business review covers business outcomes with senior leaders, usually every six or twelve months.

How long should a QBR be?

Gainsight recommends no more than an hour. A pre-read sent in advance keeps the meeting on decisions rather than presentation.

Do all customers need a QBR?

No. Most firms run them for their largest or most strategic accounts and use lighter, often digital, reviews for smaller ones.

Sources and notes

  • Gainsight, The Essential Guide to Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs), last modified 22 August 2025. Vendor guide; figures it quotes from third parties are not verified here.
  • Gainsight, How to Run an Executive Business Review That Drives Impact, 6 December 2022. Vendor blog; frequencies are recommendations, not benchmarks.
  • Gartner, Gartner Survey Reveals 60% of Technology Buyers Involved in Renewal Decisions Regret Nearly Every Purchase They Make, 14 June 2023. Analyst survey of 1,503 respondents at firms with $50m+ revenue; technology purchases only.
  • Demand Gen Report, Gartner Survey: 73% of CSOs Prioritizing 2025 Growth from Existing Customers, 20 May 2025. Trade press report of a Gartner survey of 243 sales leaders.

Next move

Pull the notes from your last three QBRs with your largest account and list every goal agreed in them. If you cannot say which were met, start the next QBR by grading them with the customer.
